summary.en: English has no single future tense. Use **will** for instant decisions, predictions and promises: _I'll help you._ Use **be going to** for plans and for predictions based on evidence: _Look at those clouds, it's going to rain._ Use the **present continuous** for arrangements: _I'm meeting Sam at six._ Use the **present simple** for timetables: _The flight leaves at nine._
summary.es: No equivale solo a nuestro futuro simple. Para planes, intenciones y cosas ya organizadas se usan going to y el present continuous; will es para decisiones del momento, promesas y opiniones.

form: **Will**: subject + will + base verb (_I'll call you_); negative **won't**
**Be going to**: subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb
**Present continuous**: subject + am/is/are + -ing, with a future time
**Present simple**: for timetables and schedules (_The course starts on Monday_)
After _when_, _if_, _as soon as_ and _before_, use the present simple for the future: _I'll call you when I arrive_

uses.text: **Instant decision, offer or promise** → _The phone's ringing. I'**ll** get it._
**Plan or intention** → _We'**re going to** repaint the hall in the spring._
**Prediction with evidence now** → _Watch out! You'**re going to** spill that._
**Fixed arrangement** → _I'**m seeing** the dentist on Thursday at ten._

note.en: A time and a person usually show it is arranged.
note.es: Suele haber hora y persona concretas: algo ya acordado.

uses.text: **Opinion or guess about the future** → _I think prices **will** go up next year._

mistakes.wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
mistakes.right: I'll call you when I arrive.

why.en: After when, if, as soon as and before, the future is expressed with the present simple.
why.es: Tras when, if, as soon as, before: presente, no will.

mistakes.wrong: Tomorrow I go to the dentist.
mistakes.right: Tomorrow I'm going to the dentist.

why.en: A personal arrangement needs the present continuous or going to, not the present simple.
why.es: Un plan personal no se dice con presente simple como en español.

mistakes.wrong: Look at the sky. It will rain.
mistakes.right: Look at the sky. It's going to rain.

why.en: A prediction based on what you can see now takes be going to.
why.es: Predicción con evidencia presente: be going to.

examples.en: I'm flying to Dublin on Friday. I've already got my ticket.
examples.es: Voy a Dublín el viernes. Ya tengo el billete.

examples.en: I'll carry that bag for you.
We're going to move to a bigger flat next year.
The conference starts at nine and finishes at five.
Don't worry, I won't tell anyone.
She's going to have a baby in June.
I think it'll be a difficult winter for many families.
As soon as the results come out, I'll let you know.
What are you doing this weekend?
If it rains, we'll cancel the picnic.

practice.prompt: I've bought a new bike. I ___ it to work from now on.

explanation.en: A plan already made: be going to.

practice.prompt: There's no milk. OK, I ___ some from the shop.

explanation.en: A decision made at the moment of speaking: will.

practice.prompt: I'll text you as soon as the train ___ .

explanation.en: After as soon as, use the present simple for the future.

practice.prompt: We ___ our new neighbours for dinner on Saturday. It's all arranged.

explanation.en: A fixed arrangement with a time: present continuous.
